t: Classic scene: the air compressor room
html:
In the app

File → New Project… → Air compressor room opens the room with its tags made and an empty program, and its guided track (Guided: the air compressors) on. File → Load Reference Solution: Air compressors loads the program of this chapter.

Two 50 HP screw compressors discharge through their check valves into a header and a 400-gallon receiver with a pressure transmitter, a high-pressure switch, a relief valve and a timed drain. The plant draws air from the receiver, and the program keeps the pressure up with as little running as it can: a lead unit on a band from 100 to 115 psi, a lag unit on a lower band from 90 to 110 that comes in only when the lead cannot keep up, the lead swapped after every cycle so the run hours share out, HAND / OFF / AUTO on each unit, and a high-pressure trip at 125 psi that latches until Reset. The relief valve at 135 psi is there for a program that misses it.

The program, routine by routine

The index, and Init on the first scan

A main routine of JSRs: Init on the first scan, then the pressure bands, the sequence, the units, the hours, the drain and the alarms. Init clears the trips and starts with C1 as the lead.

Run it
  • Run: C1 leads after the first scan

The pressure bands

Sys_OK from the selector, the E-Stop and the trips; the lead band on under 100 psi and sealed in to 115; the lag band lower, 90 to 110; a transmitter that reads under 5 or over 160 psi for two seconds is a failed transmitter.

Run it
  • The lead band comes on (Lead_Call)
  • …and drops at 115 psi

Lead, lag, and the swap

Each time the lead completes a cycle (its band drops) Lead_Sel steps on and the other unit leads; a failed lead hands the lead band to the lag; C1_Cmd and C2_Cmd come from the bands and which unit leads.

Run it
  • The lead swaps to C2 after a cycle
  • A surge brings the lag in: both run

The contactors, HAND / OFF / AUTO, run feedback

Each contactor runs in AUTO on its command and in HAND regardless, never past the E-Stop, the trip, its overload or its own failure; a contactor that closes without its run feedback in three seconds fails the unit.

Run it
  • C1 runs (C1_Run)

Run hours

A one-second pulse on the run feedback counts seconds; the hours are the seconds over 3600.

Run it
  • C1_Sec counts

The drain

Two seconds open every minute, from two timers.

Run it
  • The drain opens

The high-pressure trip, Reset and the lamps

The trip from the transmitter at 125 psi or from the switch, latched; Reset under 120 psi with the switch open; a failed unit resets once its overload does; a flasher for the lamps.

Run it
  • Put C1 in HAND and let it run up: the trip stops both units
  • …back to AUTO, wait for 120 psi, RESET

Running, and what to break on purpose

Let the plant draw: the lead cycles between 100 and 115 psi, the lag comes in on the surges, the lead swaps every cycle and the hours share out. Then break it: trip C1's overload, kill C2's starter coil, fail the transmitter high or low, open a big leak, jam the drain open, kill the high-pressure switch — and see which ones the program catches.

Watch for

A band is a seal-in with its bottom as the start and its top as the stop. Leave the top out and the unit runs until the relief valve lifts; leave the seal-in out and it chatters on and off at the bottom of the band.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE INDEX. Init on the first scan; then every scan: the bands, the sequence, the units, the hours, the drain, the alarms
rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung runs the routine Init.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. JSR(Init) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Init. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.
pats.think: a running order on a clipboard: the main routine reads it top to bottom, and each line sends you to a page that does one job.
pats.watch: A new routine does nothing until a JSR calls it. If a routine’s rungs never highlight online, look here first.

rungs.head: Init · Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: no trips carried over from before the power blink, C1 leads

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: HP_Trip is unlatched, Xmtr_Fault is unlatched, C1_Fail is unlatched, C2_Fail is unlatched, Cycled is unlatched and Lead_Sel is written.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches HP_Trip (High-pressure trip: 125 psi on the transmitter or the switch. Latched: Reset under 120 psi with the switch open), unlatches Xmtr_Fault (The transmitter reads out of range (over 160 or under 5 psi) for 2 s), unlatches C1_Fail (C1 failed: its overload, or no run feedback 3 s after its contactor closed. Reset clears it), unlatches C2_Fail (C2 failed, as C1_Fail), unlatches Cycled (The lead has run this cycle: when Lead_Call drops the lead is swapped) and puts 0 into Lead_Sel (Which unit leads: 0 = C1, 1 = C2. One added every completed lead cycle, back to 0 at 2).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(HP_Trip) Output Unlatch does: unlatches HP_Trip. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Xmtr_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Xmtr_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(C1_Fail) Output Unlatch does: unlatches C1_Fail. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(C2_Fail) Output Unlatch does: unlatches C2_Fail. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Cycled) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cycled. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(0,Lead_Sel) Move does: puts 0 into Lead_Sel. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears HP_Trip when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Bands · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE SYSTEM may run in AUTO: the selector on AUTO, the E-Stop healthy (its contact is normally closed: 1 while healthy), no trip, a transmitter that reads in range

pred.q: Sys_Sel_Pos2 is on, EStop_OK is off, HP_Trip is on and Xmtr_Fault is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Sys_OK is off. It stops at XIC(EStop_OK).

rungs.words: When Sys_Sel_Pos2 (Sys_Sel Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position) is on, EStop_OK (EStop OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is on, HP_Trip (High-pressure trip: 125 psi on the transmitter or the switch. Latched: Reset under 120 psi with the switch open) is off and Xmtr_Fault (The transmitter reads out of range (over 160 or under 5 psi) for 2 s) is off, the rung turns Sys_OK (The system may run in AUTO: the selector on AUTO, the E-Stop healthy, no high-pressure trip, the transmitter healthy) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Sys_Sel_Pos2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_Sel_Pos2 is on.
  2. XIC(EStop_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when EStop_OK is on.
  3. XIO(HP_Trip) Examine If Open asks: true when HP_Trip is off.
  4. XIO(Xmtr_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Xmtr_Fault is off.
  5. OTE(Sys_OK) Output Energize does: turns Sys_OK on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Bands · Rung 1
rungs.comment: THE LEAD BAND: on under 100 psi and sealed in until 115. A band, not a setpoint: a compressor started and stopped on a single number would cycle every few seconds
rungs.words: When either (Pressure (Air Pressure: Receiver pressure from the transmitter, psi (0-200)) is less than 100) or (Lead_Call (The lead band: on under 100 psi, off at 115) is on), Pressure is less than 115 and Sys_OK (The system may run in AUTO: the selector on AUTO, the E-Stop healthy, no high-pressure trip, the transmitter healthy) is on, the rung turns Lead_Call on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Pressure,100) Less Than asks: true when Pressure is less than 100.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lead_Call) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lead_Call is on.
  2. LES(Pressure,115) Less Than asks: true when Pressure is less than 115.
  3. XIC(Sys_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_OK is on.
  4. OTE(Lead_Call) Output Energize does: turns Lead_Call on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Lead_Call on, and Lead_Call’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Bands · Rung 2
rungs.comment: THE LAG BAND, lower: the lag only comes in when the lead alone is losing (under 90) and drops out first (at 110)

pred.q: Lag_Call is on, Sys_OK is on and Pressure is 90. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lag_Call is on.

rungs.words: When either (Pressure (Air Pressure: Receiver pressure from the transmitter, psi (0-200)) is less than 90) or (Lag_Call (The lag band: on under 90 psi, off at 110) is on), Pressure is less than 110 and Sys_OK (The system may run in AUTO: the selector on AUTO, the E-Stop healthy, no high-pressure trip, the transmitter healthy) is on, the rung turns Lag_Call on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Pressure,90) Less Than asks: true when Pressure is less than 90.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lag_Call) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lag_Call is on.
  2. LES(Pressure,110) Less Than asks: true when Pressure is less than 110.
  3. XIC(Sys_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_OK is on.
  4. OTE(Lag_Call) Output Energize does: turns Lag_Call on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Lag_Call on, and Lag_Call’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Bands · Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE TRANSMITTER CHECK: a receiver at under 5 psi with the plant running, or over 160 (past the relief valve), is a transmitter that has failed, not a pressure. Trust it for two seconds, no longer
rungs.words: When either (Pressure (Air Pressure: Receiver pressure from the transmitter, psi (0-200)) is greater than 160) or (Pressure is less than 5), the rung runs the timer T_Xmtr (Transmitter range check: 2 s) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. GRT(Pressure,160) Greater Than asks: true when Pressure is greater than 160.
    Path 2
    1. LES(Pressure,5) Less Than asks: true when Pressure is less than 5.
  2. TON(T_Xmtr,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Xmtr toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Xmtr counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

pats.t: A window, not a value.
pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.
pats.think: meeting a train. You cannot stand at one exact inch of track and wait for it to stop there; you watch the whole platform.
pats.watch: An EQU on a measured value (a position, a level, a weight) may never be true: the value jumps from just under to just over between scans.

rungs.head: Bands · Rung 4

pred.q: T_Xmtr.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Xmtr_Fault is left as it was. It stops at XIC(T_Xmtr.DN).

rungs.words: When T_Xmtr.DN (the done bit of T_Xmtr: Transmitter range check: 2 s) is on, the rung latches Xmtr_Fault (The transmitter reads out of range (over 160 or under 5 psi) for 2 s) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Xmtr.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Xmtr.DN is on.
  2. OTL(Xmtr_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Xmtr_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Xmtr_Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE LEAD SWAP: note that the lead has run…

pred.q: Lead_Call is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cycled latches on.

rungs.words: When Lead_Call (The lead band: on under 100 psi, off at 115) is on, the rung latches Cycled (The lead has run this cycle: when Lead_Call drops the lead is swapped) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Lead_Call) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lead_Call is on.
  2. OTL(Cycled) Output Latch does: latches Cycled on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Cycled stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 1
rungs.comment: …and when its band drops, swap: the two units share the hours and the starts
rungs.words: When Lead_Call (The lead band: on under 100 psi, off at 115) is off and Cycled (The lead has run this cycle: when Lead_Call drops the lead is swapped) is on, the rung unlatches Cycled and makes Lead_Sel (Which unit leads: 0 = C1, 1 = C2. One added every completed lead cycle, back to 0 at 2) = Lead_Sel + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Lead_Call) Examine If Open asks: true when Lead_Call is off.
  2. XIC(Cycled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cycled is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cycled) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cycled. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. ADD(Lead_Sel,1,Lead_Sel) Add does: makes Lead_Sel = Lead_Sel + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cycled when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 2

pred.q: Lead_Sel is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lead_Sel is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at GEQ(Lead_Sel,2).

rungs.words: When Lead_Sel (Which unit leads: 0 = C1, 1 = C2. One added every completed lead cycle, back to 0 at 2) is at least 2, the rung puts 0 into Lead_Sel.
rungs.ltr:
1. GEQ(Lead_Sel,2) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Lead_Sel is at least 2.
  2. MOV(0,Lead_Sel) Move does: puts 0 into Lead_Sel. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 3
rungs.comment: C1 leads on 0, C2 on 1
rungs.words: When Lead_Sel (Which unit leads: 0 = C1, 1 = C2. One added every completed lead cycle, back to 0 at 2) equals 0, the rung turns C1_Lead (C1 is the lead this cycle) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Lead_Sel,0) Equal asks: true when Lead_Sel equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. OTE(C1_Lead) Output Energize does: turns C1_Lead on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 4
rungs.comment: A FAILED LEAD: the lag takes the lead band

pred.q: C1_Lead is off, C1_Fail is on and C2_Fail is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lead_Fail is on.

rungs.words: When either (C1_Lead (C1 is the lead this cycle) is on and C1_Fail (C1 failed: its overload, or no run feedback 3 s after its contactor closed. Reset clears it) is on) or (C1_Lead is off and C2_Fail (C2 failed, as C1_Fail) is on), the rung turns Lead_Fail (The lead unit has failed: the lag runs on the lead band) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(C1_Lead) Examine If Closed asks: true when C1_Lead is on.
    2. XIC(C1_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when C1_Fail is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(C1_Lead) Examine If Open asks: true when C1_Lead is off.
    2. XIC(C2_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when C2_Fail is on.
  2. OTE(Lead_Fail) Output Energize does: turns Lead_Fail on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 5
rungs.comment: C1 is asked for as the lead on the lead band, as the lag on the lag band, or on the lead band when C2 (the lead) has failed
rungs.words: When either (C1_Lead (C1 is the lead this cycle) is on and Lead_Call (The lead band: on under 100 psi, off at 115) is on), (C1_Lead is off and Lag_Call (The lag band: on under 90 psi, off at 110) is on) or (C1_Lead is off, Lead_Fail (The lead unit has failed: the lag runs on the lead band) is on and Lead_Call is on), the rung turns C1_Cmd (The program asks for C1 (in AUTO)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(C1_Lead) Examine If Closed asks: true when C1_Lead is on.
    2. XIC(Lead_Call) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lead_Call is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(C1_Lead) Examine If Open asks: true when C1_Lead is off.
    2. XIC(Lag_Call) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lag_Call is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(C1_Lead) Examine If Open asks: true when C1_Lead is off.
    2. XIC(Lead_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lead_Fail is on.

pred.a: The rung is true: T_C1Fb times toward its preset.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_C1Fb counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: C1_Fail stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears HP_Trip when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 9
rungs.comment: …which unit leads…
rungs.words: When C1_Lead (C1 is the lead this cycle) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Lead1_On (Lamp_Lead1 On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(C1_Lead) Examine If Closed asks: true when C1_Lead is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Lead1_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Lead1_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 10

pred.q: C1_Lead is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Lead2_On is off. It stops at XIO(C1_Lead).

rungs.words: When C1_Lead (C1 is the lead this cycle) is off, the rung turns Lamp_Lead2_On (Lamp_Lead2 On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(C1_Lead) Examine If Open asks: true when C1_Lead is off.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Lead2_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Lead2_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 11
rungs.comment: …the high-pressure trip steady (the switch alone flashing)…
rungs.words: When either (HP_Trip (High-pressure trip: 125 psi on the transmitter or the switch. Latched: Reset under 120 psi with the switch open) is on) or (HP_Switch (Air HP_Switch: High-pressure switch on the receiver: 1 at 125 psi and over) is on and Fl_Bit (The flasher bit) is on), the rung turns Lamp_HP_On (Lamp_HP On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(HP_Trip) Examine If Closed asks: true when HP_Trip is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(HP_Switch) Examine If Closed asks: true when HP_Switch is on.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_HP_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_HP_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 12
rungs.comment: …a failed unit steady, the transmitter flashing

pred.q: C1_Fail is off, C2_Fail is on, Xmtr_Fault is off and Fl_Bit is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Fault_On is on.

rungs.words: When either (C1_Fail (C1 failed: its overload, or no run feedback 3 s after its contactor closed. Reset clears it) is on), (C2_Fail (C2 failed, as C1_Fail) is on) or (Xmtr_Fault (The transmitter reads out of range (over 160 or under 5 psi) for 2 s) is on and Fl_Bit (The flasher bit) is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(C1_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when C1_Fail is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(C2_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when C2_Fail is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Xmtr_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Xmtr_Fault is on.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

HP_Trip.desc: High-pressure trip: 125 psi on the transmitter or the switch. Latched: Reset under 120 psi with the switch open

Xmtr_Fault.desc: The transmitter reads out of range (over 160 or under 5 psi) for 2 s

C1_Fail.desc: C1 failed: its overload, or no run feedback 3 s after its contactor closed. Reset clears it

Cycled.desc: The lead has run this cycle: when Lead_Call drops the lead is swapped

Lead_Sel.desc: Which unit leads: 0 = C1, 1 = C2. One added every completed lead cycle, back to 0 at 2

Sys_Sel_Pos2.desc: Sys_Sel Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position

EStop_OK.desc: EStop OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed

Sys_OK.desc: The system may run in AUTO: the selector on AUTO, the E-Stop healthy, no high-pressure trip, the transmitter healthy

Pressure.desc: Air Pressure: Receiver pressure from the transmitter, psi (0-200)

Lead_Call.desc: The lead band: on under 100 psi, off at 115

Lag_Call.desc: The lag band: on under 90 psi, off at 110

C1_Lead.desc: C1 is the lead this cycle

Lead_Fail.desc: The lead unit has failed: the lag runs on the lead band

C1_Cmd.desc: The program asks for C1 (in AUTO)

C2_Cmd.desc: The program asks for C2 (in AUTO)

C1_HOA_Right.desc: C1_HOA Right: 1 in the right position

C1_HOA_Left.desc: C1_HOA Left: 1 in the left position

C1_OL.desc: Air C1_OL: C1 motor overload relay tripped

C2_HOA_Right.desc: C2_HOA Right: 1 in the right position

C2_HOA_Left.desc: C2_HOA Left: 1 in the left position

C2_OL.desc: Air C2_OL: C2 motor overload relay tripped

C1_Run.desc: Air C1_Run: C1 motor running: the contactor's auxiliary contact (run feedback)

C2_Run.desc: Air C2_Run: C2 motor running: the contactor's auxiliary contact (run feedback)

C1_Pulse.desc: A one-second pulse while C1 runs

C2_Pulse.desc: A one-second pulse while C2 runs

Drain_Valve.desc: Air Drain_Valve: Receiver drain solenoid: open while on

HP_Switch.desc: Air HP_Switch: High-pressure switch on the receiver: 1 at 125 psi and over

Reset_PB_Pressed.desc: Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed
